title: From a nanoparticle to the Sun
subject: generic
basis: Diameter only, across all objects. Particle diameters are historical nominal reference-material sizes; sports balls are representative, celestial bodies approximate. Idealized particle surfaces and circular celestial silhouettes. Object spacing is illustrative, not astronomical distance.
context: From a nanoparticle to the Sun

items.label: Gold nanoparticle
items.note: NIST RM 8013 nominal 60 nm gold particle. Idealized sphere; color illustrative, not a microscope photograph.

items.label: Polymer microbead
items.note: NIST SRM 1961 nominal 30 micrometre polystyrene sphere; idealized material visualization.

items.label: Golf
items.note: Representative 42.7 mm ball; R&A specifies a minimum 42.67 mm, not a fixed universal diameter.

items.label: Basketball · Size 7
items.note: FIBA 2024 equipment table 1: Size 7 circumference 750–770 mm; representative midpoint divided by pi.

items.label: Moon
items.note: NASA fact-sheet diameter, rounded to kilometres.

items.label: Earth
items.note: Equatorial diameter; local Blue Marble-derived map and cloud layer projected onto a sphere.

items.label: Jupiter
items.note: Equatorial diameter; simplified circular silhouette ignores oblateness.

items.label: Sun
items.note: Derived diameter = 2 × NASA volumetric mean radius 695,700 km. Comparisons are approximate, not precise shape models.
